title: Optimal Consumption and Investment with Energy-Efficiency Adoption
summary: This paper develops a theoretical consumption-investment model integrating energy-efficiency adoption decisions under uncertainty, proposing new definitions of rebound and backfire effects and incorporating welfare implications into optimal subsidy design. The model formalizes macro-level technology diffusion across heterogeneous agents, with a case study of a German single-family home illustrating that adoption of energy efficiency is welfare-improving and that subsidy policy can effectively steer aggregate energy consumption.
key_points: Proposes a unified framework for analyzing consumption, investment, and energy-efficiency adoption under uncertainty
Develops new definitions of rebound and backfire effects and integrates them into a model of optimal subsidy design
Formalizes macro-level technology diffusion and energy consumption across heterogeneous agents
Shows adoption threshold and post-adoption strategies depend on agent wealth, creating a channel through which financial conditions influence technology adoption
Includes a detailed case study of a representative German single-family home
Numerical analysis indicates subsidy policy effectively steers aggregate energy consumption
why_it_matters: This theoretical economics paper addresses consumption-investment theory with energy-efficiency adoption under uncertainty. While it lacks direct market trading implications, it provides frameworks relevant to energy sector analysis, climate finance, and household financial decision-making. The paper develops novel welfare analysis and subsidy design models that could inform policy-oriented finance research.
